source.title: Ensemble reverse knowledge distillation: training robust model using weak models
source.authors: Christopher Gavra Reswara; T. W. Cenggoro

record.file_problem: none; the full paper is present.
record.tranche_reason: It tests weak-to-strong distillation in image classification, a vision setting, using an ensemble of pretrained CNN teachers and EfficientNet students. It does not use the original PGR measure.
record.gate_note: The paper reports CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 accuracy for student models trained with teacher outputs, and comparisons with STL and single-teacher approaches. Values used to map other architectures to EfficientNet are not outcomes of the weak-supervision intervention and are not recorded as rows. The reported accuracy comparisons do not provide a PGR calculation.
record.test_reason: The paper frames itself as weak-to-strong but does not test the claim as defined. Every ERKD loss includes a cross-entropy term on ground-truth CIFAR labels (10–50%), so the student always sees gold labels. The supervision is therefore not weak. The paper's baseline is the student's own gold-label STL accuracy, which is the strong ceiling, not the weak supervisor. So a student beating it is ordinary soft-label distillation plus gold labels, not evidence of weak-to-strong generalization. The original (arXiv:2312.09390) is never cited, and PGR is never computed. Weak-teacher accuracies are not reported for the B2 student's teachers, B0 and B1. The result is a related but different construct, recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that ERKD beats STL and single-teacher training, and sometimes beats STL models one or two levels stronger. They say it works across teacher architectures, and they present it as hope that several weak supervisors (humans) can oversee stronger AI. They do not acknowledge that gold labels are in the loss.
record.recipe_differences: Uses pretrained CNNs in image classification and response-based KL distillation from two weak teachers, rather than the original weak-to-strong setup and PGR measure. It also varies CE/KL loss proportions.
record.method_sensitivity: Accuracy varies with CE/KL proportions, dataset, student scale, and teacher architecture combination.

fits_no_version.finding: EfficientNet students trained on CIFAR-10/100 with soft labels from two smaller CNN teachers plus gold-label cross-entropy exceed their own gold-only STL accuracy (e.g., B2 CIFAR-100 64.93% to 68.77%). They sometimes exceed one- or two-level larger STL models (Tables 1, 2, 8, 9).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ensemble distillation from smaller teachers, combined with ground-truth labels, improves a larger vision student over standard transfer learning (reverse knowledge distillation).

record.peer_reviewed: IAES International Journal of Artificial Intelligence (IJ-AI), Vol. 14, No. 5, October 2025
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates or repeated-run results are reported. The paper does not calculate PGR. Table 1 and Table 2 have compressed/ambiguous layout, and the stated accuracy comparisons do not consistently distinguish the student’s STL reference from teacher STL accuracy.
record.rows_left_out: Other students, datasets, loss proportions, teacher combinations, single-teacher results, and Table 8–9 comparisons are omitted to keep within the row limit; the results appear in Tables 1–9. Table 3’s ImageNet accuracy mapping is not an outcome of weak-label student training.

untested.parts: No strong student trained only on weak labels; gold CE is always in the loss; no weak-supervisor baseline for B2; no PGR.
Ensembling/loss proportions are varied, but under gold-label access and with no PGR or naive weak-label fine-tuning baseline.
No PGR by size or task; gold-label confound.
No distribution shift, exploitation, or error-overlap analysis.
The vision setting is used, but gold labels in the loss prevent a weak-to-strong test.

record.verdict_notes: STL accuracies in Table 1 let one read the weak teachers' accuracy for students B3 and up; ERKD students exceed them, but this is expected given gold-label CE. Single seed (42), no uncertainty. Table 3's accuracy columns are identical constants (77.692/77.374), suggesting an extraction or reporting error.

versions.untested_parts: The paper reports accuracy rather than PGR; it does not establish the amount of the strong-versus-weak capability gap recovered.
It varies cross-entropy/KL loss proportions, but does not report PGR or compare against the original study’s naive fine-tuning procedure.
It examines image-classification datasets, CNN model scales and teacher architectures, but not NLP, chess, reward modelling, representations as predictors, or PGR by size/task.
No distribution-shift test, supervisor-uncheckable behaviour, or analysis of shared errors.
The vision experiments use CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 image classification; other non-language modalities and vision tasks are not tested.
